blogs.title: Meet BLT: The Tokenizer-Free LLM That Thinks in Patches
blogs.description: A friendly tour of the Byte Latent Transformer (BLT), a new language model that learns directly from bytes—no tokenizer required. Learn how BLT groups bytes into dynamic patches based on difficulty, why that matters, and what it means for speed, accuracy, and real-world robustness.

blogs.title: Why Patches Beat Tokens: How BLT Scales Faster and Runs Cheaper
blogs.description: Break down the compute story behind BLT’s gains: fewer steps when text is predictable, more compute only when needed, and up to 50% fewer inference FLOPs at similar quality. See how BLT matches token-based models at scale and outperforms them in fixed-inference-budget scenarios.

blogs.title: Inside BLT’s Architecture: Local Bytes, Global Brains
blogs.description: A clear, diagram-free walkthrough of BLT’s three-part design: lightweight local encoder and decoder operating on bytes, and a powerful global latent transformer operating on patches. Understand cross-attention, hash n‑gram embeddings, and block-causal attention—and how they work together during training and generation.

blogs.title: Finding the Right Cut: Entropy-Based Patching Explained
blogs.description: Explore how BLT decides patch boundaries using a small byte-level language model to estimate next-byte entropy. Compare strided, space-based, and entropy-based patching, learn what ‘approximate monotonicity’ means, and see why incremental patching is crucial for generation—unlike standard BPE.

blogs.title: Tougher to Break: BLT’s Robustness on Noisy and Long-Tail Text
blogs.description: Why byte models handle messy, real-world inputs better. We unpack BLT’s gains on character-level tasks (like CUTE), phonology (G2P), and low-resource translation, plus its resilience to case flips, drops, and repeats—areas where tokenized models often fail.

blogs.title: Fixed Budget, Bigger Brains: Scaling Model and Patch Size Together
blogs.description: BLT unlocks a new scaling dimension: grow both model and patch size without increasing inference cost. See the fixed-inference scaling study, the crossover point where BLT overtakes tokenized models, and why larger patches improve with scale.

blogs.title: From Tokens to Bytes: A Practical Guide to ‘Byte‑ifying’ Your LLM
blogs.description: A practitioner’s playbook for migrating to BLT. Learn how to initialize BLT’s global transformer from a pretrained token model (e.g., Llama 3.1), set entropy thresholds, manage batching and packing, and tune for task performance—all with pointers to the open-source code.

blogs.title: Rethinking Vocabulary: Fairer, More Flexible Multilingual Models with Bytes
blogs.description: Tokenization isn’t neutral: fixed vocabularies create domain bias, brittleness, and multilingual inequities. This post explains how BLT’s tokenizer-free approach lowers these barriers, improves orthographic understanding, and generalizes better on the long tail across languages and scripts.
